Definition: from Βάττος (a proverbial stammerer) and G3056; to stutter, i.e. (by implication) to prate tediously:--use vain repetitions.
BiblicalUsage: Battologeo means to use vain repetitions, to babble on like the heathen, and Jesus warns His disciples not to pray that way, thinking they will be heard for their much speaking.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that God is not impressed by many words, and the prayer He hears is the one that means what it says.
